Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The Afghans are out in the middle. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis to open for Sri Lanka. Fazalhaq Farooqi to bowl first with a slip in place. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

Sri Lanka will be kicking themselves here, and Charith Asalanka’s call to save Dunith Wellalage for the last over, that too against Nabi backfired badly - it was only ever going to end one way. They had the perfect start with Nuwan Thushara ripping through the top order with three wickets, while Wanindu Hasaranga and Dasun Shanaka kept things tight in the middle overs to leave Afghanistan reeling at 79/6. But one miscalculation and Dushmantha Chameera's most expensive T20I spell, and suddenly the game turned on its head, with Nabi’s blitz propelling the total to 170. For Sri Lanka, the first milestone will be 101 runs to secure qualification, but they can’t afford to just play for that, as it could heap even more pressure on them. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Afghanistan were under immense pressure to put runs on the board and it showed early, as they lost three wickets inside the Powerplay. Several batters got starts, but none could kick on, with wickets tumbling regularly and 150 looking well out of reach. Then Mohammad Nabi walked in, and everything changed. He tore into the bowling, smashing it to all parts of the ground. In a breathtaking finish, Nabi hammered 46 runs in the last two, including 5 sixes in the final over, to lift Afghanistan into a commanding position.

Take a bow, Mr. President! Mohammad Nabi has earned that nickname for a reason, and once again, he lived up to it. In a do-or-die clash, when Afghanistan needed a savior, he stepped up with one of the finest T20I knocks under pressure. Blasting 60 off just 22 balls, Nabi turned the tide, powering his side to a formidable total and leaving Sri Lanka rattled despite having control for most of the innings.

OUT! RUN OUT! No six-sixes but Mohammad Nabi has scored 32 runs off the over. 8 short of his current age by the way! A yorker, outside off. Mohammad Nabi carves it to deep point. Pushes for the second run but is late at his end. The fielder, Kusal Perera throws at the keeper's end, where Kusal Mendis does the rest. Afghanistan end with 169/8. 49 runs off the last two overs. WOW!

OUT! TAKEN! Another fantastic catch from Sri Lanka! The catching has been top-notch from the Lankans, and Afghanistan slips further here. Dunith Wellalage floats it up, full and around off, Ibrahim Zadran skips down the track to loft it down the ground, but cannot quite get to the pitch of it. He still goes through the shot but has to drag it and fails to get the elevation on this one. It flies in the air towards long on where Dushmantha Chameera is standing a few yards in. Darwish Rasooli backs away and tries to ramp it away, connects well but straight towards third man. Kusal Perera, who is stationed there, judges it well and grabs it just over his head. Perera goes over the ropes, then comes back on the field to complete the catch. The third umpire is called in to check whether it is a clean catch or not, and after a few replays, it is deemed to be a fair catch. Perara's second excellent catch of the match. Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! The runs have dried up for Afghanistan, and they are finding it really difficult to find the boundaries. Ibrahim Zadran has a big role to play for them, as he has to anchor this innings and stay till the end. This wicket is not easy to bat on, and the Afghans will have to target something around 150, which will be a fighting score on this wicket. Sri Lanka have been superb with the ball, with Nuwan Thushara destroying the top order of the Afghans, and then the spinners also keeping the runs in check. They know a couple more wickets, and they can wrap things up pretty quickly here.

Commentary.Commentary: The Afghan innings is about to get underway, with Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal opening the batting. Nuwan Thushara will bowl the first over for Sri Lanka. Afghanistan will be looking to start strong and set a solid foundation for their chase of a spot in the Super 4s. Let's see how the opening pair performs against the Lankan bowlers.

The match is about to begin, and the players from both Afghanistan and Sri Lanka have gathered in the middle for a pre-match ceremony. The match officials are also present as the national anthems of Afghanistan and Sri Lanka are about to be played, marking a moment of respect and patriotism before the intense competition.

Now that Afghanistan is batting first, let's see what scenarios can happen in Group B, and what each team needs to do to qualify. Well, Bangladesh can only wait, watch, and hope that the result goes their way. For Sri Lanka, it is simple - win and qualify. However, they can also qualify with a defeat but will need to avoid losing by more than 70 runs or so, depending on the total (let's say Afghanistan make 150 runs, then Sri Lanka have to score at least 84 runs. For Afghanistan, they have to win - there is no other option for them. Bangladesh's most realistic chance is that the Lankans beat the Afghans and knock them out. Whatever happens, we are surely in for a thrilling night, and keep your calculator by your side - you may need it.

PITCH REPORT BY MIKE HAYSMAN AND RAVI SHASTRI - The pitch report indicates that the surface has a green tinge and more grass than the adjacent pitch, which could assist fast bowlers. Despite the minimal turn, Afghanistan's spinners, known for varying their lengths, can still pose a challenge. While batting might be tough initially, it could become easier as the game progresses. The hot and humid conditions are mitigated by a gentle breeze, which should help the players. Overall, the pitch seems better suited for batting compared to the one in Dubai, with a score of around 170 potentially being a good target.

Charith Asalanka, the captain of Sri Lanka, says they would have batted first as well. Adds that they have got two in-form openers, which is a big advantage, but they would like the middle order to perform as well. Informs that they have made one change as Dunith Wellalage comes in for Maheesh Theekshana.

Rashid Khan, the skipper of Afghanistan, says that they will bat first, believing that setting a target will be crucial on this wicket. With the Super 4s qualification on the line, Khan emphasized the importance of this match and acknowledged that his team struggled with pressure in their previous game. To rectify this, they plan to focus on the basics and keep their approach simple. Given the new surface, Khan noted that while no one has played on this pitch before, Afghanistan's experience playing in Abu Dhabi will be beneficial. He expects a good batting surface and estimates that a score of around 170 or above 165 would be par. Rashid also announced two changes to the team - Darwish Rasooli and Mujeeb Ur Rahman will replace Allah Mohammad Ghazanfar and Gulbadin Naib.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamil Mishara, Kusal Perera, Dasun Shanaka, Charith Asalanka (C), Kamindu Mendis, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Nuwan Thushara, Dunith Wellalage (In place of Maheesh Theekshana).

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Sediqullah Atal, Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Darwish Rasooli (In place of Gulbadin Naib), Mohammad Nabi, Azmatullah Omarzai, Karim Janat, Rashid Khan (C), Noor Ahmad, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Mujeeb Ur Rahman (In place of AM Ghazanfar).
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Rashid Khan in this must-win clash, and Afghanistan have elected to BAT first.

Afghanistan, on the other hand, has had a mixed bag so far. Despite a thumping win over Hong Kong, they suffered a narrow defeat to Bangladesh. To advance to the Super 4s, Afghanistan needs to win this match against Sri Lanka at any cost. Their spin department, led by Rashid Khan and Noor Ahmad, will be crucial in this encounter. Azmatullah Omarzai's all-round performance has been impressive, and Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz need to step up their batting game. The stakes are high, and both teams will give their all to secure a spot in the Super 4s. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

Sri Lanka has been on a roll, topping Group B's points table with four points from two matches. They've won both their fixtures, showcasing their batting prowess, particularly with Pathum Nissanka leading the charge. Their top order is in form, and Wanindu Hasaranga's all-round skills have been a significant factor in their success. Sri Lanka's pace attack has also impressed with the new ball.

Welcome to the Asia Cup 2025 match-up between Sri Lanka and Afghanistan! After a dramatic Wednesday, this match is crucial for both teams as it will determine the remaining two teams to qualify for the Super 4s.
... MATCHDAY ...

The race to the Super Four is heating up with every passing game, and the pressure is about to hit a whole new level. We now head to Abu Dhabi for what could be the biggest clash of the Asia Cup 2025 so far. It’s Sri Lanka versus Afghanistan at the iconic Sheikh Zayed Stadium, and everything is on the line. Group B has lived up to its tag as the group of death. The competition has been fierce, unpredictable, and incredibly tight. Sri Lanka currently sit at the top with two wins from two, but their place is far from secure. Afghanistan, with one win and one loss, actually have the best net run rate in the group. That means if they win tonight, they will jump straight to the top of the table. But what happens if Sri Lanka lose? Are they out? Not quite. In that case, net run rate becomes the deciding factor, and Sri Lanka have a strong advantage there. Bangladesh, who are currently in second, have an inferior net run rate, if this clash doesn’t generate favorable outcome from this, which is, a huge loss to Sri Lanka. So here’s the simple equation. For Afghanistan, it’s a must-win game. Lose, and they are out - with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh moving on to the Super Four. But if Afghanistan win, things get a lot more interesting. A win for Afghanistan won’t automatically knock Sri Lanka out. Instead, it all comes down to the margin of defeat for the Lankans. For Bangladesh to qualify, they’ll need Afghanistan to win big - and push Sri Lanka’s net run rate below theirs. That’s the only scenario where Sri Lanka could be in trouble. Phew, so much hinges on this one particular clash. The pressure is massive, the stakes are high, and the smallest of margins could decide who goes through. Sri Lanka may be unbeaten so far, but their last outing against Hong Kong, China was anything but smooth. They had to dig deep and really grind out that win. Still, they’ll take confidence from individual performances, especially Pathum Nissanka, who has been in red-hot form. He is the only player in the tournament so far to have crossed the 100-run mark, scoring back-to-back fifties. At the other end, though, Kusal Mendis has been quiet with the bat, and their opening stand is yet to cross 30 in this competition. That is an area they’ll want to fix quickly. A big plus has been Kamil Mishara’s rise at number three. His calm, composed fifty in the last game has added depth and stability to the top order. But beyond that, the middle order hasn’t really been tested yet. They’ve had limited time at the crease, largely thanks to the top three doing the heavy lifting. With the ball, Sri Lanka have been top-notch. Nuwan Thushara and Dushmantha Chameera have set the tone early with the new ball, consistently delivering tight Powerplay spells. That early control has been well supported by Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana in the middle overs. The most telling stat. They have bowled first in both games and not allowed the opposition to post anything above 150. That shows the level of control and discipline they’ve brought to the field. They'll need to bring the same intensity again, because they are up against an Afghan side that is hurting and desperate to bounce back after their loss to Bangladesh. The talent is undeniable, but so is the pressure. There are growing whispers around whether this side tends to falter in big games, especially when chasing. Despite all the progress they’ve made over the years, here's a staggering fact. Afghanistan are yet to chase down a target of over 150 against a full-member Asian team. That tells you where the concern lies. Batting collapses have been a recurring theme, particularly in pressure matches. Against Bangladesh, they were well placed but let it slip by losing wickets in clusters. However, it’s not all gloom. Sediqullah Atal has shown real promise at the top, and Rahmanullah Gurbaz looks like he’s beginning to find his rhythm again. But the middle order remains a concern - inconsistent and under pressure, especially in chases. On the bowling front, they are loaded with spin talent. Rashid Khan and Noor Ahmad have done what they do best - choke runs and build pressure during the middle overs. But for Afghanistan to truly dominate, their seamers need to step up. A bit more control with the new ball and at the death could make a big difference in this crucial clash. So here we are. One game. Two teams. So much to play for. Sri Lanka is looking to hold on to the top spot. Afghanistan is fighting to stay alive. Expect nothing less than a fierce contest.
